top_choice_rationale: P002 (Autor, Dorn, Hanson) credits the best-identified and most mature achievement on the slate: design-based local-labour-market evidence on how import competition and technological change reshape labour demand, job polarisation and regional adjustment. Dorn is a lead co-author of the China-shock papers and also co-authored the polarisation work with Autor, so he is the better-supported third name for a single discovery. Katz's best-known education-technology work overlaps with the 2023 prize, and the skill-premium strand has uncredited co-originators, so his marginal claim is the most exposed in the P001 trio. The citation can claim only what has been shown: effects on labour demand and local adjustment, with no settled long-run magnitude and no origination of the task framework. P001 is a close and defensible second, since it covers the broader skill-premium framework, and I would not call it an error. Both are clearly preferable to no award, because the evidence is mature, replicated and consequential, and the open debates concern magnitude and persistence, not existence.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile. No co-authorship or institutional tie to Autor, Dorn, Hanson or Katz appears.
